incidents-bot: [P1] Traffic-shift failed to converge for eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 failover. Many requests still hitting eu-west-1 NLB. Paging on-call: alex.

alex (oncall): seen it, joining. tl;dr traffic-manager shows job stuck at 60% applied for ~8m.

maria (sre): noticed increased 5xx rate from eu-west-1 about ~09:12 UTC. Health checks show some backends unhealthy, but not all.

jamal (networking): looking at BGP/route propagation, there was an AS-path flap on the peering to AWS eu-west-1 a bit earlier. Could be partial route acceptance.

ryan (prod-eng): traffic-manager logs show this error repeatedly: `error applying routing delta: validation timeout waiting for region drain`

alex (oncall): can someone paste `traffic-manager status --id 0x7f` output?

maria (sre): pasting recent excerpt: ```
job 0x7f status: applying
target: us-east-1
progress: 60%
pending: 342 connections pinned
reason: conn-draining timeout
```

ops-oncall: pinned connections? that smells like NLB connection draining not completing or tcp keepalives holding.

jamal (networking): checked AS paths and route tables. Route to eu-west-1 was announced from us-east-1 for failover but eu-west peers still prefer local origin for subset of prefixes. Possibly due to prepended AS path on our failover announcements -> preference mismatch.

ryan (prod-eng): also seeing a high number of long-lived websocket connections from our customer apps in eu-west-1. k8s pods didn't finish draining due to sticky session cookies and pod lifecycle hooks.

alex (oncall): customer impact? any 99th percentile latency breach or errors seen by customers?

customer-success: some customers reported degraded chat sync and delayed replies starting ~09:10 UTC. No data loss reported yet. A few paying customers raised severity.

maria (sre): SLO alert triggered for websocket error rate in eu-west-1. We're accumulating error budget burn.

jamal (networking): quick diagnostic: `dig +short www.redwood-inference.com @8.8.8.8` returns both eu-west-1 and us-east-1 IPs. But TTLs were 300s. Route53 failover policy shows weighted policy but health checks still mark eu-west-1 as green for some IPs. Means DNS alone won't steer immediately.

ryan (prod-eng): `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running` shows many pods still on eu nodes with `terminationGracePeriodSeconds=60` but connections not dropping due to keepalive.

alex (oncall): plan options: 1) force-terminate connections on eu NLB to make traffic-manager re-evaluate; 2) temporarily lower DNS TTL and re-issue policy to favor us-east; 3) manual router override in traffic manager to cut remaining 40%.

maria (sre): prefer conservative: try NLB connection-drain reset first. Jamal, can you trigger TCP reset for NLB or bump idle timeout?

jamal (networking): NLB does not support active RST injection. I can toggle target group deregistration delay to 1s which should accelerate drain. Doing that now on eu-west-1-target-group-3.

incidents-bot: action logged: jamal changed deregistration_delay from 300 to 1 on eu-west-1-target-group-3 at 09:24:18 UTC.

maria (sre): traffic-manager progress -> now 85% applied. Still ~40 connections pending.

ops-oncall: are there NAT or TCP proxies upstream holding connections? check edge haproxy/janitor.

ryan (prod-eng): found sticky-cookie config on the ingress controller for path `/chat` with `Max-Age` long. Pushing a quick ingress reload to remove sticky cookie. Patch applied.

alex (oncall): good. keep monitoring. customer-success: please update affected customers with 'mitigating, failover in progress' message.

customer-success: sent initial message to impacted accounts, noted ETA ~10m.

maria (sre): traffic-manager now reports 100% applied and target state `us-east-1` at 09:30:06 UTC. Monitoring for residual errors.

incidents-bot: incident timeline: start 09:11 UTC, mitigation begin 09:24 UTC, traffic fully shifted 09:30 UTC. Duration ~19m.

jamal (networking): follow-up: the root cause appears to be a combination: BGP path preference anomalies + long-lived websocket sessions + sticky session config = drain not finishing which blocked automation. We'll open a ticket with routing provider and review failover AS-path policy.

ryan (prod-eng): action items: 1) change default deregistration_delay to 30s for critical LB target groups; 2) add traffic-manager guardrail to force cutover if drain exceeds X minutes; 3) add pre-shift cookie purge hook for ingress controllers.

maria (sre): going to run an eval to simulate failover in staging with longer-lived connections and edge proxies to validate the new guardrails.

alex (oncall): handoff to next on-call at 10:00 UTC. I'm going to create an incident ticket with summary + timeline and tag postmortem. Anyone else want to add notes?

customer-success: customers acknowledged update. No new escalations after shift.

jamal (networking): I'll coordinate with cloud provider on AS-path propagation and see if they can remove our prepends during failover announcements.

ryan (prod-eng): adding runbook changes now to include `check-ingress-sticky` and `nuke-targetgroup-drain` commands.

alex (oncall): thanks team. I'll file the PM and assign postmortem owners: maria (lead), jamal (networking), ryan (prod-eng).

incidents-bot: incident created: INC-2198765432, severity P1. Postmortem scheduled for 48h.

maria (sre): quick note — total customer impact window ~20m, estimated affected requests ~0.8% of global traffic.

alex (oncall): handed off to ops-oncall for watch. Signing off. :wave:
